payload.title: [tenant-app-isolation-4] WebSocket app partition is client-selected via advertised schemaId with no per-principa...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING tenant-app-isolation-4 (medium/authz, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/sync/gateway.ts
LINES: 1041-1052 (Hello → findBySchemaId → client.appId), 485-491 (#storageAppId)

WHAT: At Hello, the connection's storage appId is derived purely from the client-advertised `clientCapabilities.schema.schemaId` (gateway.ts:1042-1044 `this.#appRegistry?.findBySchemaId(advertisedSchemaId)`), then pinned with `client.appId = this.#storageAppId(targetAppId)`. The schemaId is not a secret (it's returned from `GET <basePath>/schema` and embedded in every app's published schema). There is no check anywhere (grepped authz.ts, authz/rbac.ts, session-store.ts) that the authenticated principal is actually entitled to that app — appId is never part of the session/principal. The HTTP boundary derives appId server-side from the URL path (server.ts:1154-1167) and is not affected.

IMPACT: An authenticated client can advertise any other app's schemaId in its Hello frame to pin its WS connection to that app's storage partition, then read (subscribe/object snapshot/stream page) and write (object upsert/append/presence/signal) that app's data — bounded only by its own tenantId and the existing per-record/policy-hook authz, which are tenant-scoped and app-agnostic. If apps are intended as a trust boundary between distinct products sharing a tenant namespace, this lets a user of app A reach app B's partition. If apps are only a routing/namespacing convenience for the same trust domain, this is by design; the app-id.ts doc comment ('an app can neither read nor write another app's objects') overstates the guarantee.

SUGGESTED FIX: If apps are a security boundary, gate the Hello app selection on a per-principal/app-membership check (e.g. an allowed-apps claim on the session or a grant lookup) and reject a Hello whose principal is not entitled to the matched app; otherwise document explicitly that appId is a namespacing axis, not an authorization boundary.
